price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: teammate drive preceding a pick-and-roll (same-possession sequence)
universal ('any') claim versus an average effect
drive gravity / drive-and-kick effects on screen actions
methodological_questions: Can a teammate drive and a later PNR be reliably identified within one possession from PBP and derived labels?
Is any PNR PPP difference after a drive confounded by shot clock, player, lineup, opponent or survivorship?
Do derived labels (foul leakage, proxy calibration, OTHER bucket) create artifacts in PPP comparisons?
What sample size, heterogeneity and multiplicity handling does an 'any drive' claim need?
Does a placebo or negative-control predecessor event produce the same PNR PPP difference?

historical_evidence.finding: Label backfill verification ended FAIL: PNR share 28.7% against a 20-28% band, 3100 games with team PNR >33%, team identity FAIL, 2024-25 PULL_UP near 0-1% for many teams. 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated. PNR PPP 0.948 passed.

Label accuracy audit overall FAIL: OTHER 20.2% vs a <10% target, 40.8% low confidence, DRIVE foul-draw rate 1.7% vs a 14-22% benchmark, foul possessions leaking into OTHER. The record says the label issues 'undermine adaptation findings'.

OTHER PPP was inflated by 36% foul endings, DRIVE sat 12pp below the foul benchmark, PNR showed a 22% foul rate, and only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) mapped to a real play type via initiation_type.

Shot-level PBP-derived PNR share of half-court shots ranged from 7.567% (OKC) to 13.824% (IND) in 2024-25. These rates were a calibration input to a PBP proxy PNR whose possession-level share is about 17.9-19.6%.

Season stability of top suppressors and sequential premiums: only 2/30 stars were stable. The record cites negative DRIVE->PNR sequences, e.g. Giannis->Lillard -0.263 (n=31), with min n=20 per cell. The record text was cut in the retrieval result and was not read in full.
Star-specific suppression gaps were found with no placebo or matching. The record notes that later sequence work treated similar star-chain gaps as artifacts.
DRIVE PPP was 1.198 in the regular season vs 0.912 in the playoffs (-0.286, 25 teams) and PNR was -0.173. Regular-season and playoff play-type PPP therefore differ materially, with no CIs.
PNR PPP rose +0.087 across playoff series buckets (observational, selection caveats, no CIs).
A powered null in the strictest fixed-effects test. Naive and DiD contrasts (+0.140, +0.090) were explained by selection of high-PPP play types.
Observed on-ball coverage labels were unusable (14.9% and 3.3% labeled) and switches_on was unpopulated. This is relevant to defensive context for PNR.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Backfilled play-type labels (including proxy-calibrated PNR) as a trustworthy basis for play-type analysis
failed_approaches.why: Label/classification error. Distribution and team-identity checks failed, and 82.8% of PNR labels were proxy_calibrated.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Inferred play-type labels as a reliable measurement of DRIVE, PNR and OTHER
failed_approaches.why: Systematic label issues, foul leakage and low confidence were recorded.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing PPP across play-type labels as if the differences were real efficiency
failed_approaches.why: Foul-ending leakage inflated or deflated PPP by label, and initiation_type mapped only 0.7% of possessions. The family was labeled artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Naive and DiD contrasts of PPP across play types
failed_approaches.why: Selection of high-PPP play types explained the gaps; only the fixed-effects test was informative, and it was null.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Descriptive star/lineup gap findings without placebo or matching
failed_approaches.why: No placebo or matching; later sequence work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

evidence_establishes: Earlier work records the play-type labels (DRIVE, PNR, OTHER) as having serious, documented labeling problems: foul leakage, proxy calibration of PNR, and failed distribution and identity audits.
Earlier work recorded a naive-contrast failure mode: PPP differences between play types or contexts can arise from selection or labeling rather than from the factor of interest.

Earlier sequential DRIVE->PNR evidence is limited to a few star-pair cells with n around 31 and a stability rule failed by 28 of 30 stars. It does not show a general positive effect, and the cited DRIVE->PNR cells it names are negative.
No retrieved record directly tests whether a teammate drive preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP across the league.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether drive-preceded PNRs have higher PPP than other PNRs once shot clock, player, lineup and opponent are controlled.
Whether PBP can identify 'a drive preceding a PNR' within a possession, since the retrieved records do not describe the label structure for chained actions.
Whether the negative DRIVE->PNR cells in FAM:SF-APPA-058 are real or noise. The full text was not read and the record is a stability test.
own_inferences: As posed ('any' drive), the claim is universal. It would be falsified by credible heterogeneity, and it cannot be 'supported' by a pooled average alone. It should be restated as an average effect with a heterogeneity check.

The PNR label is partly proxy-calibrated and the DRIVE label has foul leakage. A drive-then-PNR flag may be partly constructed from the same events that determine outcomes and shot-clock position, so a spurious positive or negative is plausible.

Survivorship: drives that produce a shot or foul end the possession and cannot precede a PNR. Drives that kick out and reset into a PNR are selected for being unproductive, which would bias toward a negative association. Later-clock PNRs also have mechanically different PPP.
Because past naive contrasts were explained by selection, a raw PPP difference should be treated as uninformative without matching or fixed effects.
The most likely competent-test outcomes are artifact or an inconclusive result, not a clean positive.
uncertainties: Whether the possession graph stores more than one action label per possession, so that a drive-then-PNR sequence is represented at all.
The exact contents of FAM:SF-APPA-058 beyond the truncated text, and the related families FAM:SF-APPA-001 and FAM:SF-APPA-005, which were not read.
Whether a calibration-free PNR definition can be built from the PBP fields listed.
The 2025-26 regular season is complete from 2026-04-13, but 2025-26 playoff data on 2026-06-14 are partial and will complete on 2026-06-21. Playoff results should not be mixed with partial data.
Defensive coverage labels are unavailable (FAM:SF-APPS-058), so the defensive scheme confounder cannot be controlled.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history, I would have considered proceeding with a matched PPP comparison on the existing labels. The retrieved records show those labels failed audits (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPM-014, FAM:SF-CHT-025), PNR is mostly proxy-calibrated, and naive PPP contrasts were previously artifacts (FAM:SF-APPM-016). That moved the decision to do_not_proceed as posed, with a reduced, validated minimum viable test.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR is 82.8% proxy-calibrated and DRIVE has foul leakage, so the drive-then-PNR flag and PNR PPP are measured with known systematic error (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPM-014, FAM:SF-CHT-025).
Foul endings and shot outcomes affect which bucket a possession falls in (FAM:SF-CHT-025), so the labels depend on the outcome being measured.
Shot clock, player, lineup, opponent and coverage determine both the existence of a prior drive and PNR PPP. Coverage labels are unusable (FAM:SF-APPS-058).

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests the league-wide effect of a preceding teammate drive on PNR PPP. Adjacent work covers star-pair DRIVE->PNR premiums (rejected as stable, n around 31) and documents label and selection artifacts that would affect this test.

risks.text: Proxy-calibrated PNR and leaky DRIVE labels could misclassify both exposure and outcome.
Play-type buckets depend on possession endings such as fouls, which also determine PPP.
Elapsed shot clock, initiator and screener quality, lineup, opponent and defensive coverage.
Drives followed by a reset PNR are a selected subset, since productive drives end the possession. Player- and team-level cells can also show regression to the mean.
A later start of the PNR in the shot clock constrains time and shot quality for drive-preceded PNRs.
Drive-then-PNR sequences are probably rare; stratified cells (as in FAM:SF-APPA-058 at n around 31) are underpowered.
An 'any drive' claim invites many strata (player, team, season, drive type).
Without a placebo predecessor (non-drive action), any difference cannot be separated from ordinary sequence context (FAM:SF-CHT-009).
Regular-season and playoff PPP differ materially (FAM:SF-APPS-011), and labels differ across seasons (e.g., 2024-25 PULL_UP near 0%).
Chaining logic and proxy calibration could produce duplicates or mis-ordered events.

design.estimand: As posed ('any' teammate drive raises PNR PPP), the claim is not testable as a universal. The minimum viable test is the within-matched-stratum difference in PNR PPP between PNR possessions with a teammate drive earlier in the same possession and matched PNR possessions without one, plus the heterogeneity of that difference across drive-initiator strata.
design.unit: Half-court PNR possession (a possession with a validated PNR event), clustered by game and team-season.
design.sample: Complete data only: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular seasons and playoffs, plus the 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13). Exclude the 2025-26 playoffs (partial on 2026-06-14). Include only PNRs from a hand-audited, non-proxy-calibrated PBP rule. Exclude possessions with foul-bucket leakage or run the analysis with and without them. Treat regular season and playoffs separately.
design.power: Not computed, because sequence counts are unknown. First step: count qualifying drive-then-PNR possessions overall and per stratum. Proceed only if at least about 2,000 exposed possessions exist for the pooled test, and require a minimum detectable effect of at most 0.05 PPP (PPP SD per possession about 1.1 assumed; SE with 2,000 exposed and matched 2,000 controls is about 0.035, so MDE is about 0.1, which would likely be insufficient unless the sample is much larger). Do not run stratum-level tests with fewer than 200 exposed possessions per cell.
design.controls: Matching or fixed effects on shot-clock elapsed at PNR start, period and score state, initiator, screener, lineup and opponent. Exclude possessions where the drive ended in a shot or foul. Use team-season fixed effects, fit the contrast within each team-season, and use a cluster bootstrap by game. Use PBP shot-level outcomes (points and foul-adjusted free throws) rather than label-derived PPP where possible. Pre-register the PNR identification rule and audit a random sample of at least 300 sequences by video or manual play review to estimate misclassification.
design.falsification: Placebo exposures: a preceding non-drive action (e.g., a pass or off-ball movement) with matched timing, expected to show no effect. Negative control: PNR PPP before the drive time window, or shuffled drive labels within team-season. Check that the label-audit pass rates (foul-draw rate, OTHER share) meet the benchmark before analysis, and abort if not. Replicate in a held-out season and compare with FAM:SF-APPM-016-style fixed-effects results.
design.multiplicity: One primary pooled test. Heterogeneity strata (initiator type, drive outcome, season) are secondary and corrected with Holm or Benjamini-Hochberg at q=0.05. Report the number of strata tried.
design.decision_rule: Supported (average effect) only if the pooled matched difference is positive with the 95% CI excluding zero, survives fixed effects, is robust to label-audit exclusions, shows no placebo effect, and replicates in the held-out season. Rejected if the CI is within +/-0.03 PPP of zero with adequate power. The universal 'any drive' claim is not supported if any adequately powered stratum shows a CI entirely below zero. Report artifact if the effect disappears under matching or placebo. Otherwise report inconclusive. Do not run the analysis if the label-audit precondition fails.
design.data_version: Freeze the per-game NBA stats API files and the derived possession graph as of 2026-06-14, with the 2025-26 regular season complete (2026-04-13) and the 2025-26 playoffs excluded. Record the label-build version, the PNR proxy calibration version and a hash of the data.

research_concepts: drive-and-kick / gravity effect on screen actions
methodological_questions: Can a drive be reliably identified and attributed as preceding a PNR within the same possession from play-by-play data?
Is the PNR PPP difference after a teammate drive confounded by possession context, player quality, lineup, or shot clock?
Does derived play-type labeling introduce outcome-derived labels or label error affecting PPP comparisons?
What sample size, exposure and multiple-testing considerations apply to a universal 'any drive' claim?
args.query: Does any teammate drive preceding a pick-and-roll raise PNR points per possession, and how reliable are play-type labels and sequence definitions for testing this?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- explore_graph(node_id): the relationships of one graph node (a family or a question, method, dataset, measure, limitation or risk node), with neighbour labels.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-06-14, in the area of play-type labeling and data quality):
Any teammate DRIVE preceding a PNR raises PNR PPP.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

reasoning_details.text:
I'm weighing whether to pull one more family record, since the Giannis-to-Lillard drive-to-pick-and-roll figure (-0.263 on 31 samples) looks directly relevant. The earlier result got cut off, though I have enough to wrap up now, so I'm leaning toward finishing without another lookup.

I'm going through the status labels I recorded for each family, noting which were rejected, inconclusive, supported, or untestable. The claim that any teammate drive before a pick-and-roll raises its PPP is universal, and the Giannis-to-Lillard case, though based on only 31 samples, points the other way. The pick-and-roll labels are also mostly proxy-calibrated, so I'm weighing whether a clean test is even possible with the raw play-by-play data.

I'm settling on a recommendation of not proceeding as the question is posed, since the "any" claim can't be cleanly tested and the pick-and-roll labels are mostly proxy-calibrated, with a reformulated minimum viable test as the fallback. I'm also assigning rough probabilities across supported, rejected, untestable, artifact, and uncertain outcomes. Data timing is a concern too: the 2025-26 playoffs are incomplete relative to the question date, so I'd freeze to completed seasons plus the regular season, and I need to check whether drive labels might depend on the outcome.

I'm checking whether possession chains might hold only one label, which would hide a drive that comes before a PNR in the same possession. I'm also noting selection effects, since drives that end in a shot or foul never reach a PNR, and a design that matches on shot-clock time, lineup, and opponent, with game-level bootstrapping and placebo comparisons, could help isolate the "any drive" effect.

I'm now setting the decision rule: I'd treat the universal "any drive" claim as rejected if even one well-powered stratum has a lower confidence bound below zero, and I'd check multiplicity with Holm or Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the drive-passer strata, summarizing the overall effect as a pooled average plus heterogeneity.
